conclusion.label: endorses

report:
## Conclusion

The claim is **well-supported by evidence, not false**. The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix) demonstrably reduces shingles (herpes zoster) risk in adults aged 70 and older.

## Evidence

The pivotal evidence comes from the ZOE-70 randomized, placebo-controlled phase III trial, specifically designed to test RZV in adults 70 years of age or older. Published in the *New England Journal of Medicine*, this trial found that the vaccine's efficacy against herpes zoster in adults 70+ was similar to that seen in younger cohorts—high and statistically significant (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800; corroborated at https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/).

A pooled analysis combining ZOE-50 and ZOE-70 data specifically for the ≥70 age subgroup showed vaccine efficacy of 91.3% against shingles (https://agsjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/jgs.16917). This is consistent with the original ZOE-50 trial in adults 50+, which found the related HZ/su vaccine "significantly reduced the risk of herpes zoster," with "vaccine efficacy in adults who were 70 years of age or older similar to that in the other two age groups" (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184).

Long-term follow-up data extending to 11 years post-vaccination (ZOE-LTFU trial, published in *eClinicalMedicine*) confirm that efficacy against herpes zoster remains high over time in this population, including the original ZOE-70 placebo recipients who were later vaccinated (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(25)00173-7/fulltext).

Real-world post-licensure effectiveness data published in *The Lancet Healthy Longevity* further corroborate these trial findings outside controlled settings (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanhl/article/PIIS2666-7568(22)00039-3/fulltext).

## Bottom line

Multiple high-quality, peer-reviewed randomized controlled trials and long-term follow-up studies consistently show strong efficacy of RZV in adults 70+. There is no credible evidence in these sources contradicting the claim.
